recognize_zh: 四顆嗜中性球的細胞質幾乎看不到顆粒、呈淡灰透明（hypogranular），核分葉異常：左上一顆為多葉且形狀不規則，其餘為 C 形或兩三葉；背景紅血球可見淚滴形與碎片，符合 MDS 的顆粒球發育不良（dysgranulopoiesis）。
features: Four neutrophils with markedly hypogranular, pale grey cytoplasm
Abnormal nuclear segmentation: one hypersegmented, irregularly lobulated nucleus (upper left) and others with C-shaped or two-to-three-lobed nuclei
Small cytoplasmic vacuole in the upper-left neutrophil
Red cells with teardrop forms, fragments and elliptocytes; platelets not seen in the field
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows four neutrophils with striking cytoplasmic hypogranularity and abnormal nuclear segmentation, including an irregular hypersegmented form and several with C-shaped or bilobed to trilobed nuclei. Toxic granulation and Döhle bodies are not present. The red cells show poikilocytosis with teardrop cells and occasional fragments, and platelets are not seen in this field, in keeping with the reported thrombocytopenia. In the context of known TP53-mutated MDS, the findings are consistent with dysgranulopoiesis.

ddx.dx: Smear preparation or storage artifact (EDTA delay)
ddx.vs: Storage artifact causes nuclear lobe rounding and cytoplasmic vacuolation in all cells, whereas true hypogranularity persists in freshly prepared smears and accompanies cytopenias.
Megaloblastic neutrophils are large and hypersegmented but retain normal granulation, with macro-ovalocytes and low B12/folate.

ddx.dx: Acquired or reactive hypogranularity (e.g., SARS-CoV-2 infection, drugs such as mycophenolate)
ddx.vs: Reactive hypogranularity is transient and occurs without cytogenetic or molecular evidence of clonality.
